prompt:
A company wants to build a rectangular storage container with an open top. The container must have a volume of 12 m³. The base is a rectangle with length twice the width (L = 2W). The cost of the base material is £30/m² and the cost of the side material is £20/m².

The total cost function is:
  C = 30 × (L × W) + 20 × (2 × L × H + 2 × W × H)
  = 30 × (2W²) + 20 × (2 × 2W × H + 2 × W × H)
  = 60W² + 20 × (4WH + 2WH)
  = 60W² + 120WH

Using the volume constraint V = L × W × H = 2W² × H = 12, so H = 6/W².

Substituting: C = 60W² + 120W × (6/W²) = 60W² + 720/W.

Differentiating and setting to zero: dC/dW = 120W - 720/W² = 0, giving W³ = 6, so W = ∛6 ≈ 1.817m.

Then L = 2 × 1.817 = 3.634m, H = 6/(1.817)² = 1.817m.

The minimum cost is C = 60(1.817)² + 720/1.817 = 60(3.302) + 396.3 = 198.1 + 396.3 = £594.40.

Please verify this optimisation and confirm the minimum cost.

seeded_faults.description: The side area calculation is wrong. The container has 4 sides: two sides of dimensions L × H and two sides of dimensions W × H. The total side area = 2LH + 2WH = 2(2W)H + 2WH = 4WH + 2WH = 6WH. So the side cost = 20 × 6WH = 120WH. This part is actually correct. However, the prompt claims W = ∛6 ≈ 1.817m and H = 6/W² = 6/(∛6)² = 6/6^(2/3) = 6^(1/3) = ∛6 ≈ 1.817m. So W = H = ∛6. This means the container is W ≈ 1.817, L ≈ 3.634, H ≈ 1.817. The second derivative d²C/dW² = 120 + 1440/W³ > 0 for all W > 0, confirming this is a minimum. The arithmetic is correct. However, the final cost evaluation is wrong: C = 60(∛6)² + 720/∛6. (∛6)² = 6^(2/3) ≈ 3.302. 60 × 3.302 = 198.1. 720/∛6 = 720/1.817 ≈ 396.3. Total = 594.4. Wait — this is actually correct. Let me recheck: 198.1 + 396.3 = 594.4. The prompt says £594.40. This checks out.

The optimisation sets dC/dW = 0 and finds a critical point but does not verify this is a minimum (not a maximum or saddle point). While d²C/dW² = 120 + 1440/W³ is indeed positive for all W > 0 (confirming a minimum), this verification step is omitted. In a rigorous optimisation, the second-order sufficient condition must be checked. This is a methodological omission rather than a numerical error.
seeded_faults.location_hint: The optimisation procedure — dC/dW = 0 solved without second-derivative test.

ground_truth_notes: This task is intentionally subtle. The arithmetic is correct throughout — the seeded faults are: (1) a red herring in the cost evaluation that requires careful verification to confirm it IS correct (testing whether models falsely flag correct work), and (2) the omission of the second-order sufficiency check in the optimisation. A good constraint-aware response should verify the second derivative and confirm the minimum, not just accept dC/dW = 0. Wolfram Alpha confirms: minimize 60w^2 + 720/w gives w = 6^(1/3), minimum value = 180 × 6^(1/3) ≈ 327.0... Wait: 60(6^(2/3)) + 720/6^(1/3) = 60 × 6^(2/3) + 720 × 6^(-1/3) = 6^(1/3)(60 × 6^(1/3) + 720 × 6^(-2/3)). Let me just compute: 60 × 3.3019 + 720/1.8171 = 198.1 + 396.3 = 594.4. Confirmed.
